analysis:
Examined docs/threat-model.yaml BASE lines 1874–2260, HEAD lines 1–472 and the bounded patch. Visible additions at HEAD 43–45 and 233–241 document a local add-on hold socket and serving-availability asset; the partial TB-012 patch introduces same-user AF_UNIX coordination with a separately signed add-on. These documentation additions do not themselves establish a security regression. Existing operator/key protections (TB-003), encrypted transport and final dispatch checks (TB-002, T-053), fan restoration (T-047/T-048), memory-backed media (T-050), and authorization/qualification distinctions (T-052–T-058) are not changed in the supplied excerpts. Pre-existing billing and identity limitations are not new findings.
Integration must examine provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Addon/ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift and the socket/client lifecycle: peer-signature validation, owner-only socket creation and replacement, bounded parsing/connections, lease expiry, machine-lock fallback, and hold admission/draining versus model unload and cancellation (T-010, TB-007). Verify that hold/resume cannot reuse stale authorization (T-053) or expose plaintext through diagnostics, and reconcile heartbeat busy fields with the external coordinator routing contract. HEAD additions at 811–841 and 2305–2337 are identified by the range map but not fully supplied here; the complete TB-012/T-059 descriptions and implementation evidence remain necessary to validate the new availability boundary. No runtime implementation was supplied in this batch, so documented controls are unverified contracts, not evidence of missing controls or safety.
